Ultrametric trees with given imbalance and branching-time parameters

Source: R/simulate.R
sim_tree_shape.Rd

Draws the topology with rtopology_beta() and the internode intervals with intervals_lineage_rate(), and combines them with assign_ages(). The topology and the intervals are drawn independently, the gamma statistic depends only on the intervals and the Colless index only on the topology, so for a given n the realized gamma depends only on c (or rate) and the realized Colless index only on beta. To draw trees near target values of both statistics, see sim_tree_target().

Usage

sim_tree_shape(
  n,
  beta = 0,
  c = 0,
  nsim = 1,
  root_age = 1,
  rate = NULL,
  sampling_fraction = 1
)

Arguments

n

Number of tips, a single integer of at least 2.

beta

Aldous' beta, a single finite number greater than -2. Lower values give more imbalanced trees.

c

Lineage dependence of the split rate, a single finite number.

nsim

Number of trees.

root_age

Age of the root (positive).

rate

NULL (the default), to use c, or a vectorized function of the number of lineages k that returns the per-lineage split rate. It must return n - 1 positive, finite values for k = 2, ..., n, and cannot be combined with a c other than 0.

sampling_fraction

Fraction of the tips of the complete tree that are kept, a single number greater than 0 and at most 1.

Value

With nsim = 1, a binary, ultrametric phylo object with root depth root_age; otherwise a multiPhylo object with nsim such trees. Attribute params holds beta, c (NA with rate), root_age and sampling_fraction, and attribute rate holds the rate function, if any.

Details

With sampling_fraction below 1, a complete tree of round(n / sampling_fraction) tips is drawn, beta and c (or rate) apply to that tree, and n tips are kept at random, so the result still has n tips and root depth root_age. Incomplete sampling removes recent splits and so lowers gamma (Pybus & Harvey 2000), so gamma no longer follows the calibration of calibrate_shape(). After sampling, gamma also depends slightly on the topology, because the splits that remain depend on it, so the separation between gamma and the Colless index is exact only for complete trees. A rate function must be valid for the number of tips of the complete tree.

Very extreme values of c (or rate) make some intervals negligible relative to the others, and the corresponding branches round to length zero; a warning is given when this happens.

Reproducibility

The same seed gives the same trees on the same platform. Between platforms (for instance, arm64 and x86-64), differences in the last bit of floating-point functions can change a few draws of the topology, so trees may differ.

References

Pybus, O. G., & Harvey, P. H. (2000). Testing macro-evolutionary models using incomplete molecular phylogenies. Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 267, 2267–2272. doi:10.1098/rspb.2000.1278

Examples

set.seed(1)
tr <- sim_tree_shape(50, beta = -1, c = -1)
ape::gammaStat(tr)
#> [1] -4.320064
trees <- sim_tree_shape(50, beta = -1, c = -1, nsim = 10, root_age = 30)
# logistic slowdown towards a carrying capacity of 60 lineages
sim_tree_shape(50, rate = function(k) 1 - k / 60)
#> 
#> Phylogenetic tree with 50 tips and 49 internal nodes.
#> 
#> Tip labels:
#>   t1, t2, t3, t4, t5, t6, ...
#> 
#> Rooted; includes branch length(s).
# 50 tips sampled from a complete tree of 100
sim_tree_shape(50, sampling_fraction = 0.5)
#> 
#> Phylogenetic tree with 50 tips and 49 internal nodes.
#> 
#> Tip labels:
#>   t1, t2, t3, t4, t5, t6, ...
#> 
#> Rooted; includes branch length(s).
